findings.title: No cache recheck after acquiring the write lock (missing double-checked locking)
findings.body: After the RLock fast path fails, GetWebAssets acquires the exclusive lock and unconditionally re-reads the manifest from disk/CDN and overwrites entryPointAssetsCache. If N concurrent requests arrive before the cache is populated (e.g. at startup in non-Dev mode), every one of them performs the file read serially instead of one goroutine populating the cache and the rest reusing it. The fix is incomplete double-checked locking: after taking the write lock, the function should re-read entryPointAssetsCache and return it if non-nil (for the non-Dev case).

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file I/O and CDN HTTP request
findings.body: GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu (write lock) for the entire duration of readWebAssetsFromFile and, if a CDN URL is ever set, the blocking HTTP request in readWebAssetsFromCDN (currently the cdn variable is hardcoded to "", but that is an existing call path). In Dev mode this happens on every call. A slow or hanging CDN request would block every other caller of GetWebAssets, including the RLock fast-path readers, stalling request handling. Consider loading the result outside the lock and only taking the lock briefly to publish it.
